newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Futures fell Australian stocks by close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Futures fell Australian stocks by close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2493 -18 US 30yr cl 6.55 +0.02
10yrbond futs 92.675 -0.040 Gold NY 344.45 Lon fix 346.00
*Stocks end lower despite early record high, futures-linked selling slashes leaders in afternoon. Volume 448.52 million, value A$999.38 million, 1,147 traded, 338 steady, 415 up, 394 down.
Australian shares closed lower on Wednesday despite an early record high as futures-linked selling slashed the leaders in the afternoon session.

By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 10.7 points lower at 2,491.0 after peaking at 2,508.3, surpassing the previous record high of 2,506.5 reached on February 14. The March share price index futures contract was 18 points lower at 2,493, a 2.00 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said while the day had been largely characterised by choppy, trendless trade, arbitrage players had ventured out in the afternoon to send some of the leaders tumbling.
"There was not too much going on, although there was a lot of arbitrage taking place," said broker Martin Angel of Perth-based broker Eyres Reed.
Results, and their impact, continued to be the focus for many individual stocks.

Underlining this was the continuing slide of soft drink maker C-C Amatil, whose shares slid 70.5 cents to A$11.485 as brokers continued to downgrade the stock after Friday's soft year net profit result of A$142.1 million.
"Their shares are still going downhill. The valuation is still hard to justify," said a Sydney-based dealer.

FAI Insurances shares inched a cent higher to 71 cents after a 35.5 percent higher first half net profit of A$7.8 million, while Hoyts Cinema exhibited their maiden half year results, posting a net profit of A$12.2 million, seeing their shares dip a cent to A$2.67.
Property developer Mirvac Ltd failed to build on a 17.6 percent higher first half net profit of A$13.69 million, its shares closing a cent lower at A$2.49.
Shares in gold miner Sons of Gwalia added four cents to A$7.24 after a nine percent higher first half net profit of A$18.15 million.
Goldfields Ltd shares firmed a cent to A$2.10 despite a 17.4 percent fall in first half net profit to A$3.56.

Shares in West Australian-based pastoral and energy house Wesfarmers Ltd soared to a record high of A$10.45 on strong volume as investors took an upbeat view of its growth prospects following last week's strong first half profit.
Hancock & Gore's 1-for-4 scrip takeover bid lifted the lid on troubled milliner Leutennegger Ltd's share price, which jumped 47 percent to 28 cents.
Rises barely shaded falls, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade picked up as did futures activity with arbitrage trade the feature.
Total options traded 44,300 (37,325)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 8,934 (6,543)
In other local markets, Australian bonds ended softer after trading in tight ranges and hoping for a more definite lead from U.S. Treasuries after today's January U.S. CPI report.

The market had a minor flutter to the downside after January merchandise imports came in much stronger than expectations, but the move was not sustained in relatively light trade. By 5.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.31 percent.
The Australian dollar eked out a meagre US$0.7635/7675 range for a fourth straight session Wednesday, and dealers suspected its inability to sustain a rally presaged a renewed downtrend.
Bulls were especially disappointed at the failure to capitalise on Tuesday's robust economic outlook from the Reserve Bank which extinguished all thoughts of a near term easing.
By 5.45 p.m. (0645 GMT), the local dollar was hard pressed at US$0.7636/41 having eased from US$0.7667/72 late here Tuesday.
